title: Two-bay frame with beams pinned to the outer columns: beam moment and shear

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: AISC, Manual of Steel Construction - Allowable Stress Design, 9th ed. 1989 (no page given) - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Two bays of 18 ft, columns 10 ft; columns 12 in x 24 in (I = 13,824 in^4), beams 12 in x 30 in (I = 27,000 in^4), every member A = 1e7 in^2 (the page's listing: axial deformation suppressed), E = 30,000 ksi. Outer column bases fixed, centre column base pinned. The two beams are continuous over the centre column and moment-released at the outer columns (the listing's member releases). Load case 1: 50 kip on the outer column tops, 100 kip on the centre column top, 100 kip at midspan of each beam; load case 2: 10 kip/ft on both beams. Targets at the middle of the first beam; in load case 1 the shear is the value on the side of the centre column (the page's section at 0.501 of the span). Units kip, in. First-order analysis. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
